titulek: Russia planned ‘false flag’ operation with mass casualties on Polish territory, Rzeczpospolita reports
titulekPuvodni: Russia planned ‘false flag’ operation with mass casualties on Polish territory, Rzeczpospolita reports
shrnuti: Russian intelligence services planned a sabotage operation on Polish territory for late October or early November, senior sources told the Polish newspaper Rzeczpospolita. The plan could have involved crossing the border and staging an attack on a target inside Poland.

vyrez.text:
Russia planned ‘false flag’ operation with mass casualties on Polish territory, Rzeczpospolita reports — Meduza
Skip to main content
Russia planned ‘false flag’ operation with mass casualties on Polish territory, Rzeczpospolita reports
November 18, 2026, 9:26 am
Source: Rzeczpospolita
Russian intelligence services planned a sabotage operation on Polish territory for late October or early November, senior sources told the Polish newspaper Rzeczpospolita. The plan could have involved crossing the border and staging an attack on a target inside Poland.
They said the sabotage could have been staged as a “false flag” operation meant to pin the blame on Kyiv.
The warning about the planned sabotage came from intelligence services in partner countries, though analysts at Polish intelligence agencies also raised the possibility of a provocation, the newspaper’s sources said. Rzeczpospolita reported that similar warnings were sent to intelligence services in the Baltic states: Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania.
“We had information about specific sites where the attack was supposed to take place. The Russians were counting on a large number of casualties,” one of the newspaper’s sources…

The Norwegian Armed Forces are deploying an aerial surveillance system in the town of Kirkenes, near the Russian border, to detect drones that stray off course at an early stage.

The government noted that the measures are preventive and are not linked to any specific new threat.
The sensors are designed to detect drones, warn of their presence and provide a comprehensive picture of all activity in the airspace over border areas.

No drone crashes were reported.

Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB) arrested the former head of a state-run youth patriotism center in Moscow on suspicion of stealing public funds earmarked for its programs, the RBC news outlet reported Friday, citing two people familiar with the case.
Yelena Belikova, who ran the Russian Center for Patriotic Education until September, faces up to 10 years in prison on a charge of large-scale embezzlement. The FSB is investigating the case.
Moscow’s Lefortovsky District Court on Thursday barred Belikova from contacting other defendants or witnesses in the case, sending or receiving mail and using the internet.
Belikova stepped down as director on Sept. 2, according to the SPARK corporate database. Her former deputy, Dmitry Stepyko, is now serving as acting director.

Článek
Po ukrajinském zásahu bytových domů v Ruskem okupované Luhanské oblasti v noci na pátek zahynuli nejméně tři lidé. Dalších šest lidí, včetně dítěte, bylo zraněno. Na platformě Telegram o tom informoval Moskvou dosazený šéf oblasti Leonid Pasečnik. Ukrajinské útoky hlásí také Smolenská oblast, kde byl zasažen například průmyslový objekt. Tam se zásahy zřejmě obešly bez zranění.
Pasečnik uvedl, že lidé v zasažených domech, kde se zřítily betonové panely, v době útoku spali. V současnosti se ví o třech mrtvých a šesti raněných, z nichž jednoho záchranáři vyprostili z trosek. Mezi zraněnými je také osmiletá dívka. Pasečnik napsal, že v troskách stále mohou být lidé.
Vasilij Anochin, gubernátor ruské Smolenské…

shrnuti: Polish military officials are examining two suspected airspace violations following a powerful blast in Lublin Voivodeship during Russia's large-scale attack on Ukraine. An unidentified object was found to have fallen near a village.

Poland investigates possible airspace breaches after explosion near Ukrainian border | Ukrainska Pravda
Aircraft. Stock photo: Getty Images
A powerful explosion was recorded in the village of Chmielek in Poland's Lublin Voivodeship on the morning of 20 November during a large-scale Russian attack on Ukraine's west. The Polish military is investigating "two possible violations" of the country's airspace and has dispatched emergency response teams to the scene.
Source: European Pravda; PAP ; RMF24 ; Polsat News ; Defence24 ; Onet
Details: CCTV footage from the vicinity of the village of Chmielek in Biłgoraj County appeared on social media on the morning of 20 November, showing a flash and capturing the sound of a loud explosion.

Lieutenant Colonel Jacek Goryszewski, spokesperson for the Operational Command of the Polish Armed Forces, confirmed to Polsat News that the military is investigating "two possible violations" of Polish airspace.
He said the incidents had been recorded at approximately 06:30.

Tartu is allocating €33,000 for five portable power stations to help Lviv maintain essential services during widespread blackouts.
The city will purchase the units in cooperation with the Estonian Refugee Council, with the equipment intended to help Lviv keep essential services running during power outages. The funding will come from the City of Tartu's reserve fund.
As winter approaches, Tartu and the Refugee Council are working closely to get the equipment to Lviv as quickly as possible. Mayor Urmas Klaas (Reform) noted that the colder months make the power outages Ukrainians continue to face during the war even harder to endure.
"We want to help Lviv prepare for disruptions so that essential services remain available to residents even in difficult conditions," Klaas said.

A cyberattack targeting the public website of municipal transport company Tallinna Linnatransport (TLT) on Monday compromised the personal data of several thousand people, the company said.
The attack exploited a security vulnerability in software used on the website after a plugin update had not been installed. The attacker downloaded a copy of the website's database.
The incident affects 2,440 TLT employees. The leaked data included employees' names, job titles and personal identification numbers.
An initial investigation has also found that an additional 2,370 people who had submitted their information through forms on the tlt.ee website may have been affected. The exposed information may include names and email addresses entered into those forms.

Evropskou komisi zasáhl rozsáhlý kybernetický útok, který mohl ohrozit osobní údaje jejích zaměstnanců. Hackeři podle serveru Politico využili nástroj umělé inteligence k odhalování zranitelnosti v počítačových systémech. Útok narušil fungování některých interních služeb Komise a jeho plným rozsahem se úřady stále zabývají. Útok byl podle bruselského serveru natolik závažný, že se jím ve středu během svého pravidelného jednání zabývali i eurokomisaři.

The Crimean Bridge has been attacked by Ukraine for the third time this week, Russia has said.
The Moscow-installed head of Crimea, Sergei Aksyonov, said that traffic was temporarily suspended following another strike on the bridge connecting Russia to occupied Crimea.
The critical bridge had already been hit twice earlier in the week resulting in severe damage and part of the bridge collapsing into the water.
The important infrastructure has long been targeted by Ukraine because of its significance as a logistical and symbolic asset to Moscow's war effort.

Moldova’s foreign ministry summoned the Kremlin’s ambassador-designate in Chișinău, Oleg Ozerov, on Wednesday morning after Russian drones violated the country’s airspace. 
Seven drones entered Moldova’s airspace Tuesday afternoon, the country’s defense ministry said , including one over the capital Chișinău. At least five of them crashed on Moldovan territory.
“This is what the ‘peace’ promoted by the Kremlin looks like: attack drones flying over the capital of a free and sovereign state,” the foreign ministry said in a statement . “Russia does not respect the Republic of Moldova or its people and is putting their lives at risk.”

Russia’s combined drone and missile attack on Tuesday was detected in 44 locations in Ukraine, according to Ukraine’s air force .

Hungary is halting rail traffic to and from Ukraine for two days after a Russian drone attack hit the western Ukrainian city of Mukachevo, Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar said on Nov. 17.
A drone came down around 300 meters from Ukrainian Mukachevo railway station, Magyar said , prompting the evacuation of the crew of a train arriving from Hungary. The suspension will affect the Austria–Ukraine rail connection, Magyar said.
Russia has in recent months increased drone attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure close to the borders of other European countries.

Stretching across the Kerch Strait in the Black Sea, the Crimean Bridge was always a symbol: for Russia, a prestige project cementing its claim to sovereign Ukrainian territory, and for Ukraine, a hated piece of infrastructure emblematic of Moscow's occupation of the Crimean Peninsula.
A key section of the double-arched, 12-mile-long bridge now lies on the seabed, brought down by an arsenal of Ukrainian long-range weaponry in a seven-stage operation culminating in a dramatic collapse.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov has said that the bridge "will be rebuilt, and it will be even better than before".
But eight years after its unveiling, the bridge has now become material proof of Kyiv's ability to pierce through Moscow's military defences to hit even its most treasured and protected structures.

November 17, 2026, 3:07 pm
Source: Parlamentskaya Gazeta
Russia’s government has submitted a bill to the State Duma that would establish special bankruptcy procedures for war participants: mobilized soldiers and those who have signed military contracts.
Under the bill, if an arbitration court grants a bankruptcy petition, property worth up to 10 million rubles would be excluded from the “bankruptcy estate” (all of a debtor’s assets subject to sale to repay creditors). The court would decide which property qualifies.
The bill’s explanatory note states that the legislation “has a high social orientation, reflected in the implementation of special support measures” for Russians who have signed military service contracts.
“An analysis of court practice shows it would be worthwhile to codify the proposed approaches,” the bill’s authors added.
